criteria.label: Call-handling hiring
criteria.why: A contractor hiring dispatchers, customer service reps or a call center is paying people to answer and book calls right now, which is exactly the work the product takes on. This is the strongest "needs help now" signal.

criteria.label: Hiring activity
criteria.why: A contractor adding technicians is adding jobs to book and calls to answer, and a business that is hiring at all has the busy season or the backlog that makes missed calls expensive.

criteria.label: Multi-site
criteria.why: A contractor with several locations takes calls for several service areas, and one deal covers all of them.

criteria.label: Web presence
criteria.why: A live website means an operating business taking inbound calls from customers who found it online; those are the calls that go to voicemail after hours.

criteria.label: Business type
criteria.why: Confirms the listing is a residential trade contractor, not a supply house, manufacturer or adjacent business the search returned. Google's category is self-chosen by the business, so it is evidence, not proof.

criteria.label: Tech posture
criteria.why: A contractor already paying for hiring software buys tools to fix operational problems, so a software conversation is not a first.

anon_note: Public demo data. Business names, addresses, phone numbers and websites are replaced with placeholders, role counts are shown as ranges, and each business's hiring system is hidden. Scores, signals and generated text are real output from one sample run.
